landing.hero.subheadline: Join the AI zombie trend: upload two photos and get a 15-second scored zombie film — no prompts to write, nothing to edit, no watermark. One-time credit packs, as low as {price} per film.
landing.hero.note: Renders in about 3 minutes. You can close the tab meanwhile.
landing.shot.title: One Film, Four Shots
landing.shot.subtitle: Every zombie love story that broke the internet follows the same shot list:
landing.shot.s1.title: The Cabin
landing.shot.s1.desc: A tight close-up on a tearful face behind a raised handgun, while the zombified loved one walks closer through a dark, dusty cabin.
landing.shot.s2.title: The Undead Face
landing.shot.s2.desc: An extreme close-up: pale grey skin, cloudy eyes, bared teeth — frightening, yet still unmistakably the person you recognised in photo two.
landing.shot.s3.title: The Choice
landing.shot.s3.desc: The gun lowers and falls away. Both arms open in invitation — and the zombie breaks into a sprint and leaps.
landing.shot.s4.title: The Match Cut
landing.shot.s4.desc: Mid-air, the cabin becomes a golden wheat field at sunset. The same leap lands as an embrace, both of them alive again.
landing.how.title: How the Trend Works
landing.how.step1.title: Upload Two Photos
landing.how.step1.desc: You and your partner, you and your pet, or two friends — clear faces work best.
landing.how.step2.title: Pick a Style
landing.how.step2.desc: Love story, pet, friends or Halloween party — each with its own soundtrack and pacing.
landing.how.step3.title: Pay with Credits
landing.how.step3.desc: One-time packs, as low as {price} per film. If a render fails, your credits come back automatically.
landing.how.step4.title: Get the Film
landing.how.step4.desc: A 15-second, scored, watermark-free MP4 ready for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.
landing.how.photos.title: How to pick the two photos
landing.how.photos.p1: Same two people in both frames. Photo one hands the model the survivor, photo two the one who has turned — two unrelated images leave it with nobody to carry across the four shots.
landing.how.photos.p2: Match the framing. Keep the distance, head height and angle close; a wide shot into a close-up reads as a jump cut.
landing.how.photos.p3: Light both photos alike. The film already plans its own turn from cold cabin light to golden sunset, so matching your two inputs keeps the faces continuous instead of forcing a relight on top of them.
landing.how.photos.p4: Give each photo its role. Photo one is the survivor — the face behind the raised gun; photo two is the one who has turned, the face the extreme close-up finds.
landing.how.photos.p5: Order is casting. Photo one becomes the survivor, photo two the undead — swap them and the gun is held by the wrong face.

landing.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
landing.faq.q1: What is the AI zombie trend?
landing.faq.a1: A viral format where two photos become a 15-second mini film: one of you has already turned, the other raises a gun and cannot bring themselves to fire, and the leap that follows hard-cuts into an embrace in a golden wheat field — cinematic, scored to a trending song. It has blown up across TikTok, and you can now make your own from any two photos.
landing.faq.q2: How many photos do I need?
landing.faq.a2: Exactly two. Front-facing, well-lit faces give the most recognizable result.
landing.faq.q3: How long does a render take?
landing.faq.a3: Usually 2–4 minutes. The film keeps rendering even if you close the tab — it waits in your library.
landing.faq.a4: Credits are refunded to your balance automatically. You never pay for a film you did not get.
landing.faq.a5: Yes. Photos are used only for your render and deleted within 24 hours. They are never used to train models.
landing.faq.a6: No. One-time credit packs, as low as {price} per film — buy once, use whenever the trend comes back around.
landing.faq.q7: How is this different from a general video model?
landing.faq.a7: A general model has no ceiling, but the prompt, the edit, the soundtrack and the per-platform export are all yours — hours on the first try. Here the scene templates are already tuned on the server: two photos, one story, a film in about three minutes. For a 40-second multi-scene piece, the general-model route suits you better.
landing.faq.a8: A template site gives you a zombie look on one photo — fast, with almost no decisions. This trend is a four-shot film carried by two identities: how the survivor and the one they love are held through the cabin and the wheat field. The grade and the soundtrack are done in one pass here, and the people, outfits and pacing belong to your film alone.
